info.title: JellyPass household app API
info.description: The household app API, /jellypass/app/v1, on household hosts only. info.version is GET /me's apiVersion. v1 only ever gains fields and endpoints; see docs/app-design.md, "Native clients (contract)". Schemas are closed (additionalProperties false) so the server's own test catches an undeclared field; a client decodes leniently and ignores fields it does not know. Every answer is Cache-Control: no-store.

householdHost.description: The household's own address (host, and port if it is not 443), as its administrator mapped it: any hostname. The household is decided from it; a host that is no household's is answered 421 unknown_host.

post.description: The entry leaves the caller's list and the title can be asked for again; what happens to the Seerr request is decided in the background and never shown (see docs/app-design.md, "Cancelling (step 2c)"). Counted against the Get this budgets. An ID the household does not list, or an entry that cannot be cancelled (any more), gets the same 202 and nothing happens. Added in apiVersion 2.

post.summary: Not interested: hide a movie from the caller's discovery lists.
post.description: Only for the caller, in this household: it leaves their Discover lists, See all, network and studio pages (shorter pages, never refilled), stays in search results and on its title page with hidden true, and changes nothing else (My requests, Get this, playback, other members). Idempotent: hiding a title already hidden keeps when it was first hidden. TMDB is not asked. 409 hidden_limit_reached only for a new title past the caller's 2000. Added in apiVersion 3.

Unauthorized.description: 401 unauthorized: a missing, invalid or disabled token, or a member of another household, all alike.

NotFound.description: 404 not_found: an unknown path, or a title TMDB does not know. 404 household_not_found: the host is a household address no household has (no token is checked; a client signed in there treats it as the household gone).

HiddenLimit.description: 409 hidden_limit_reached: the caller already hides 2000 titles; unhide some first.

Error.description: Every error body: one of these codes, always with its own status (see the responses: InvalidRequestError, UnauthorizedError, NotFoundError, TooManyRequestsError, HiddenLimitError, UnavailableError), the same for every endpoint and every title. A client treats an unknown code by its HTTP status.

NotFoundError.description: 404: not_found on a household host, household_not_found on a legacy generated address whose household does not exist.

HiddenLimitError.description: 409: hidden_limit_reached, only from POST /hidden/movie/{tmdbId} and /hidden/tv/{tmdbId} for a title the caller has not hidden yet while they already hide 2000. Decided by the caller's own hidden titles alone.

HouseholdState.description: The household's own view of a title. A client renders an unknown value as unavailable.

CoarseStatus.description: A household request's coarse status. A client renders an unknown value as requested.

apiVersion.description: The revision of the v1 contract the server speaks: one more with each release that adds a field or endpoint, never lower. Absent before it existed (revision 0).

Play.description: Set only when state is in_library.

url.description: Exactly https://<the household host>/web/#/details?id=<itemId>; a client ignores anything else.

tmdbId.description: Any positive whole number TMDB gives, up to 2^53 - 1; only one up to 2147483647 can be opened as /movie/{tmdbId} or /tv/{tmdbId}.

posterUrl.description: TMDB poster at w342; the same file is served at other TMDB widths.

backdropUrl.description: TMDB backdrop at w780; the PWA also draws the same file at w1280.

rating.description: TMDB vote average to one decimal; null when TMDB has none.

hidden.description: Whether the caller hid this title ("Not interested"; see /hidden). Only the caller's own hides, in this household. Discovery lists leave hidden titles out, so it is true only in search results and on title pages. Added in apiVersion 3; a client decodes a missing value as false.

hasFilms.description: Whether /discover/network/{id}/films and /all are offered for it.

Sources.description: JellyPass's own allowlist, in the order Home shows it; no TMDB call, the same for everyone.

tmdbId.description: Asked for through /movie/{tmdbId}/get or /tv/{tmdbId}/get, so at most 2147483647.

byYou.description: Whether the caller made any of the household's records for the title.

cancellable.description: Whether the caller may cancel it now (POST /requests/{id}/cancel): their own request, still Requested, nothing of it ready yet and not still being sent. From the household's own records only. Added in apiVersion 2: a client that finds no such field has no cancel.

requestedOn.description: The day (UTC, YYYY-MM-DD) the household last asked for the title; never a time. Added in apiVersion 2.

Requests.description: The household's own titles from Get this, newest first.

Accepted.description: The same answer whatever happens to the title.

Hidden.description: The answer to hiding (true) or unhiding (false) a title: the same whether or not it was hidden before.

hiddenAt.description: When the caller first hid it (UTC, ISO 8601, milliseconds).

HiddenPage.description: A page of the caller's own hidden titles, newest first, 50 a page: IDs only, named by the client as My requests' titles are. A page past the last is empty with nextPage null.
